text.p: - Elected members of parliament from the rightist "Spring" alliance parties, comprising People's Party, Social Democrats and Christian Democrats met for the first time on Wednesday. The "Spring" parties got 45 of 90 seats in the parliament in the country's second general election on November 10.
- The board of national radio and television will elect the a new general manager from two candidates on Thursday.
- Number of retired people in Slovenia in 1996 rose 0.5 percent to 443,565, the country's pensioners' institution said. The country's total population is about two million.
- More than 26 percent of Slovenians smoke, a research study showed.
- Industry's share of Slovenia's GDP fell from over 50 percent at the end of the 1980s to about 36 percent, Minister of Economic Affairs Metod Dragonja said.
- Slovenian businessmen held a promotional video conference on Slovenian tourism with Japanese businessmen on Wednesday. Slovenian businessmen taking part in a business conference in Tokyo.
- Northwestern parts of Slovenia suffered traffic problems caused by the first snowfall, while country's coast was flooded after heavy rains on Wednesday.

- Slovenian employers said they were ready to negotiate with trade unions about changes to an agreement determining social payments. A month ago unions staged a two-hour general strike in protest against cuting social benefits.
